paper_metadata.title: Efficient option pricing with unary-based photonic computing chip and generative adversarial learning

experiments.description: On-chip training of a GAN generator to learn and load a target asset-price distribution into a unary photonic representation, evaluated on log-normal and normal target distributions with up to 8 bins.

algorithm.variant: hybrid GAN with photonic generator and classical discriminator; Wasserstein GAN training
algorithm.optimizer: gradient-free evolutionary algorithm for generator; gradient descent for discriminator
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training iterations until the fake and real distributions converge; final L2 norm stabilizes at -18 dB

optimizer_settings.generator_optimization: evolutionary optimization with selection, crossover, mutation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Asset-price distribution is binned and loaded into unary waveguide modes; each bin maps to a unary basis element.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn a generator distribution matching the real market/target distribution under a GAN min-max objective with Wasserstein training.

problem_instance.description: Distribution learning for asset-price samples used to upload probability distributions into the photonic chip.

dataset_specification.description: Target distributions are log-normal and normal; real samples are drawn from the desired probability distribution.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Binning into unary basis; fake samples are photon-path probability distributions from the generator.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of generator output distribution to target distribution; convergence tracked by L2 norm over 100 training iterations.

hardware.framework: TensorFlow for discriminator; photonic integrated circuit for generator

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Real samples drawn from target distributions; fake samples generated from photonic waveguide probabilities.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute L2 distance between generated and target distributions; monitor convergence in dB.

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment is GAN distribution learning for asset-price uploading; no explicit classical baseline metric or speedup factor is reported.

experiments.description: Unary photonic option-pricing experiment for a three-asset European option, including distribution loading, payoff calculation, and iterative amplitude estimation.

algorithm.variant: iterative amplitude estimation without phase estimation in unary encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: increase amplitude-amplification iterations m up to 50 and observe convergence of payoff standard deviation and error

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Three asset values encoded in a 3-bin unary basis; each basis element is represented by two waveguides, giving 6 waveguide inputs total including ancilla encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate European option payoff C(ST,K)=∫_K^∞ (ST-K)dST via ancilla measurement probability after payoff rotation and amplitude amplification.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection/measurement on ancilla waveguides encoding state |1> for asset prices above strike.

problem_instance.description: Proof-of-principle European option pricing with three asset values.

dataset_specification.description: Three discrete asset values; distribution derived from a log-normal model in the theory section.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Continuous asset-price distribution discretized into n bins; payoff angles normalized by maximum asset price s_max.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare theoretical payoff expectation with experimental results; track standard deviation over 50 measurements per amplitude-estimation step and payoff error versus m.

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: linear depth for distribution loading; constant depth for uploaded unitary in proof-of-concept; amplitude amplification repeated up to m=50

noise_model.mitigation_details: Post-selection strategy mentioned for unary scheme; no quantitative mitigation protocol reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize asset-price distribution into unary bins; compute payoff rotation angles θ_i from asset prices and strike.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Shift raw angles (2m+1)θ back to θ; compute payoff error and standard deviation across repeated measurements.

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation; iterative amplitude estimation on a unary photonic chip
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims quadratic speedup in the number of calls to the distribution-loading and payoff operators to reach the same confidence level; the experimental data show improved convergence of standard deviation and payoff error with increasing amplitude-amplification iterations.

scalability_data.metric_value: experimental payoff converges toward theoretical expectation with m up to 50

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(m)) for Monte Carlo scaling as stated in the paper
